acip: ,KHAMS 'OG MA GNYIS SU GZUGS LA MA LTOS PAR SEMS DE RIS DANG SROG LA MI BRTEN NAM ZHEN, MI BRTEN PA YIN TE, GZUGS KYI 'DU SHES DANG MA BRAL BAS STOBS CHUNG BA'I PHYIR, GZUGS MED KYI SEMS NI GZUGS LA MI LTOS TE, TING NGE 'DZIN GYI STOBS KYIS GZUGS KYI 'DU SHES DANG BRAL BAS STOBS DANG LDAN PA'I PHYIR,
wylie: khams 'og ma gnyis su gzugs la ma ltos par sems de ris dang srog la mi brten nam zhen, mi brten pa yin te, gzugs kyi 'du shes dang ma bral bas stobs chung ba'i phyir, gzugs med kyi sems ni gzugs la mi ltos te, ting nge 'dzin gyi stobs kyis gzugs kyi 'du shes dang bral bas stobs dang ldan pa'i phyir
english: "Well then," one might ask, "couldn't the stream of mind in one of the two lower realms then also rely on the discrete type of being involved, or upon life, without depending upon form?" It could not, because the mind in these cases is of little force, as it is not yet free of the conception of form. The mind of the formless realm, on the other hand, need not rely on form: because of the power of its single-pointed concentration, the mind is free of the conception of form and thus possesses considerable force.

acip: DE LA KHO NA RE, DE LA BYIN PA DE DE LTA BU'I PHYI PA MTHA' YAS PA LA BYIN PA BAS KYANG BSOD NAMS CHE BA MIN NAM ZHEN, BDEN MOD, 'ON KYANG SNGAR DUD 'GRO'I SKYE GNAS SU SONG BA BRGYA LA BYIN PA BAS, MI TSUL KHRIMS 'CHAL PA GCIG LA BYIN PA RNAM PAR SMIN PA BRGYA 'GYUR DU RE BAR BYA'O, , ZHES BRGYA SHA STAG GSUNGS PA'I 'DRES KYI DBANG GIS YIN PA'I PHYIR ZHES GSUNG ,
wylie: de la kho na re, de la byin pa de de lta bu'i phyi pa mtha' yas pa la byin pa bas kyang bsod nams che ba min nam zhen, bden mod, 'on kyang sngar dud 'gro'i skye gnas su song ba brgya la byin pa bas, mi tshul khrims 'chal pa gcig la byin pa rnam par smin pa brgya 'gyur du re bar bya'o, , zhes brgya sha stag gsungs pa'i 'dres kyi dbang gis yin pa'i phyir zhes gsung
english: Someone might ask whether making offerings to such a person wouldn't be a greater merit than giving to an absolutely infinite number of the non-Buddhists mentioned. Admittedly it would be, he says; the word "hundred" is employed here first to maintain a continuity in composition, since in passages of the sutra preceding the one in question the word constantly appears: "You could give something to a hundred beings living in the animal state of birth, yet still look forward to results a hundred times more powerful maturing from the deed of offering something to a single human being, even an immoral one." ******** 54 The Great Disc of Wind � �

acip: DE YANG STON PA YANG DAG PAR RDZOGS PA'I SANGS RGYAS MNYAM MED SHA'KYA'I RGYAL PO DE NYID KYIS DANG POR BYANG CHUB MCHOG TU SEMS BSKYED, BAR DU BSKAL BA GRANGS MED GSUM DU TSOGS BSAGS, MTHAR MNGON PAR RDZOGS PAR SANGS RGYAS NAS CHOS KYI PHUNG BO BRGYAD KHRI BZHI STONG GSUNGS PAR MDO SNGAGS GNYIS MTHUN KYANG,
wylie: de yang ston pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas mnyam med sha'kya'i rgyal po de nyid kyis dang por byang chub mchog tu sems bskyed, bar du bskal ba grangs med gsum du tshogs bsags, mthar mngon par rdzogs par sangs rgyas nas chos kyi phung bo brgyad khri bzhi stong gsungs par mdo sngags gnyis mthun kyang
english: Now the traditions of both the open and secret ways of Buddhism agree on certain details of how our Teacher, the fully Enlightened One, the unequaled King of the Shakyas, reached His Buddhahood.  It all started when He first reached the Wish for highest enlightenment.  In the interim then, for the length of three "countless" numbers of eons, he amassed the necessary collections of good karma.  In the end He reached his total enlightenment, and after that gave the teachings of the 84,000 heaps of the Dharma.
